recap.text: Manasa is a singer with a meter-wide cobra hood and a worm in her brain from the Valtay Corporation. She appears as a hologram on the Danger Zone, where she supports the Valtay against the Borant system. A pulse hits her trailer on Earth, and Ripper announces she has perished. Princess D'nadia reveals Manasa traded trailers with the crawlers, and a Valtay dreadnaught claims Prince Stalwart's yacht.

Princess D'nadia of the Prism Kingdom sponsors Donut, while the Valtay Corporation sponsors Carl. A brain parasite from the Valtay controlled Manasa, whom the Skull Empire killed. The Valtay slew the Maestro in retaliation for the botched assassination that killed Manasa instead of Carl.
Donut tells Princess Chandra, Esquire, that every Naga is a raging psycho. Donut thought Chandra might be nice, but she was incorrect. The only nice one was Manasa, who was a worm head.

beats.headline: A worm in a famous head
beats.text: For the record: Manasa, a silver and black cobra-headed creature whose hood is a meter wide, towers over the Danger Zone table as a hologram. The director Evo's briefing: a famed singer. A Naga, but not of the Blood Sultanate, so Crawler Donut need not kill her on the ninth floor. Not really a Naga either. The real Manasa perished long ago, and she contracted with the Valtay Corporation to keep her career going once she died. A worm in her brain, driving the body? Correct. Her career is hotter than ever. Latest single: eighth in the entire universe.
beats.gist: Manasa is a silver and black cobra-headed hologram and a famed singer.

beats.headline: On the side of the Valtay
beats.text: She laughs at Crawler Donut's put-downs of Tucker, the comedian who is not funny, forked tongue flipping in and out. On the panel's main topic, the Valtay Corporation's attempt to collect its debt from the Borant system, she is, for obvious reasons, on the side of the Valtay. Ripper and Princess D'nadia think both sides are dicks and also side with the Valtay; Tucker mostly backs the kua-tin. The three crawlers are careful to say nothing stupid about either.
beats.gist: Manasa laughs at Donut's put-downs of Tucker, a comedian with a flipping forked tongue.

beats.headline: The pulse hit her trailer
beats.text: Manasa has been removed from the broadcast. Mid-sentence from the host, her hologram blinks in and out and is gone, and the studio bucks. The report: an attack on her trailer. She was vacationing on Earth and had ascended for the interview, and the trailer was hit with a pulse. Ripper announces that it appears she has perished. Then Prince Stalwart's statement plays, announcing the crawlers Carl and Donut executed by a pulse from his personal yacht. Tucker, no longer snooty: "It was meant for you."
beats.gist: A pulse hits Manasa's trailer on Earth, and Ripper announces she has perished.

beats.headline: She offered to trade
beats.text: Princess D'nadia explains. The crawlers needed cleaning facilities, and Manasa offered to trade trailers. D'nadia weeps black oil: Manasa was her friend for countless years, worm head or not, and the Prism Kingdom is filing a grievance. Tucker supposes the Valtay must see it as an accident. Ripper: does anyone know how much money she brings the Valtay each year? Their entertainment assets outearn their technology, and they just murdered her. Then word arrives: a Valtay dreadnaught claims Stalwart's yacht; the rumor puts Queen Consort Ugloo and the former prince Maestro aboard.
beats.gist: Manasa, a pop singer, traded trailers for cleaning facilities before the Valtay murdered her.

beats.headline: Her final performance
beats.text: Ripper closes the show on a video of Manasa singing, her final performance: a cappella, in an opulent dining room, a hauntingly sad soprano. The studio watches in dead silence. Afterwards Crawler Donut says she was really nice. Over chat, Crawler Carl works it through: the crawlers were the bait, and so was Manasa, and the switch was either arranged or seized upon; it humiliates the orcs and damages their alliance with the Valtay, and his guess is that Borant benefits. Crawler Donut: MANASA HAD THE VOICE OF AN ANGEL. To Mordecai she adds that Manasa thought Mongo was adorable.
beats.gist: Ripper closes the show with a video of Manasa singing a cappella in an opulent dining room.

beats.headline: The worm and the retaliation
beats.text: Crawler Donut's first sponsor is Princess D'nadia of the Prism Kingdom, and Crawler Carl's is the Valtay Corporation. He notes that two parties present at the Danger Zone incident have sponsored them: D'nadia was very upset when the Skull Empire killed Manasa, who had really been controlled by a brain parasite from the Valtay. Further on, sorting out the Skull Empire's succession, he records the rest: the Maestro, once second in line, was disowned, then slain by the Valtay in retaliation for the botched assassination that killed Manasa instead of Carl.
beats.gist: Princess D'nadia and the Valtay Corporation sponsor Donut and Carl.

beats.headline: The only nice one
beats.text: Crawler Donut's assessment, delivered to Princess Chandra, Esquire, who has come with legal papers: every Naga the crawlers have met has been a raging psycho. For about five seconds Donut thought Chandra might be a nice one, and she was incorrect, which is sad. The only nice one was Manasa, and she was a worm head. The Nagas, Donut concludes, are doing a terrible job as ambassadors for their species.
beats.gist: Donut tells Princess Chandra that Manasa, a worm head, was the only nice Naga.
